title: CTS Psalms — Unit 11: The Psalms in Ministry I (Capstone)

blocks.en: 📖 The Book of Psalms — Unit 11: The Psalms in Ministry I (Capstone)
blocks.es_reference: 📖 El Libro de los Salmos — Unidad 11: Los Salmos en el Ministerio I (Proyecto Final)

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in Your sight." — Psalm 19:14 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Sean gratos los dichos de mi boca y la meditación de mi corazón delante de ti." — Salmo 19:14 (RVG)

blocks.en: 1. From Study to Ministry
blocks.es_reference: 1. Del Estudio al Ministerio

blocks.en: For ten units we have studied the Psalms one at a time — the two ways of Psalm 1, the Shepherd of Psalm 23, the King of glory in Psalm 24, the penitence of Psalm 51, the Word in Psalm 119, the cross in Psalm 22, the fearless trust of Psalm 56, the silence of God in Psalm 28, the blessings of Psalm 103, and the cast burden of Psalm 55. In these final two units we turn a corner. The question is no longer only "What does this psalm mean?" but "How do I now carry these psalms into the work of ministry?" The Psalms were never meant to stay on the study desk. They were Israel's hymnbook and prayer book, sung in the temple and whispered in exile, and they remain the most usable book in all of Scripture for the practical work of caring for souls.
blocks.es_reference: Por diez unidades hemos estudiado los Salmos uno por uno — los dos caminos del Salmo 1, el Pastor del Salmo 23, el Rey de gloria del Salmo 24, la penitencia del Salmo 51, la Palabra del Salmo 119, la cruz del Salmo 22, la confianza sin temor del Salmo 56, el silencio de Dios del Salmo 28, las bendiciones del Salmo 103, y la carga echada del Salmo 55. En estas dos unidades finales doblamos una esquina. La pregunta ya no es solo "¿Qué significa este salmo?" sino "¿Cómo llevo ahora estos salmos a la obra del ministerio?" Los Salmos nunca fueron destinados a quedarse en el escritorio de estudio. Fueron el himnario y el libro de oración de Israel, cantados en el templo y susurrados en el exilio, y siguen siendo el libro más utilizable de toda la Escritura para la obra práctica de cuidar las almas.

blocks.en: Psalm 19:14 (NKJV): "Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in Your sight, O LORD, my strength and my Redeemer."
blocks.es_reference: Salmo 19:14 (RVG): "Sean gratos los dichos de mi boca y la meditación de mi corazón delante de ti, oh Jehová, roca mía, y redentor mío."

blocks.en: There is a reason ministers have always reached for the Psalms first. Every other part of the Bible speaks to us — the Law commands, the Gospels narrate, the Epistles instruct. But the Psalms speak for us. They put words in the mouth of the grieving, the guilty, the frightened, the thankful, and the lost. When a person in your care cannot find words for what they feel, the Psalms have already written them. This unit considers four arenas where that gift becomes ministry: preaching, pastoral care, public worship, and the leading of others in prayer.
blocks.es_reference: Hay una razón por la que los ministros siempre han recurrido primero a los Salmos. Toda otra parte de la Biblia nos habla a nosotros — la Ley manda, los Evangelios narran, las Epístolas instruyen. Pero los Salmos hablan por nosotros. Ponen palabras en la boca del afligido, del culpable, del atemorizado, del agradecido y del perdido. Cuando una persona a su cuidado no halla palabras para lo que siente, los Salmos ya las han escrito. Esta unidad considera cuatro campos donde ese don se vuelve ministerio: la predicación, el cuidado pastoral, la adoración pública, y guiar a otros en oración.

blocks.en: 2. Preaching the Psalms
blocks.es_reference: 2. Predicar los Salmos

blocks.en: The Psalms preach differently from other texts, and the wise preacher honors the difference. A psalm is not an argument to be outlined like one of Paul's letters; it is a piece of inspired poetry meant to move the heart as it teaches the mind. To preach a psalm well, begin by finding its single dominant emotion or claim — trust, repentance, awe, lament, praise — and let that become the center of gravity for the whole message. Psalm 23 is not six unrelated points about sheep; it is one great assurance: the LORD is my shepherd, and therefore I shall not want. Psalm 51 is not a lecture on sin; it is the cry of a broken man finding his way home.
blocks.es_reference: Los Salmos predican de manera distinta a otros textos, y el predicador sabio honra la diferencia. Un salmo no es un argumento para bosquejar como una de las cartas de Pablo; es una pieza de poesía inspirada destinada a mover el corazón mientras enseña la mente. Para predicar bien un salmo, comience por hallar su única emoción o afirmación dominante — confianza, arrepentimiento, asombro, lamento, alabanza — y deje que eso sea el centro de gravedad de todo el mensaje. El Salmo 23 no son seis puntos inconexos sobre ovejas; es una gran seguridad: Jehová es mi pastor, y por tanto nada me faltará. El Salmo 51 no es una conferencia sobre el pecado; es el clamor de un hombre quebrantado hallando su camino a casa.

blocks.en: Notice, too, how often the Psalms preach Christ. We saw it most plainly in Psalm 22, where the cross is described a thousand years before it happened, but it runs everywhere: the blessed Man of Psalm 1 is fulfilled in Jesus, the King of glory of Psalm 24 enters as our Redeemer, and the Shepherd of Psalm 23 lays down His life in John 10. The preacher who handles a psalm faithfully will, like Philip with the Ethiopian, begin at the psalm and preach Jesus. And because the Psalms are so honest about human emotion, they give the preacher permission to address what people actually feel on Monday morning — fear, guilt, grief, doubt — rather than only what they are supposed to feel.
blocks.es_reference: Note, también, con cuánta frecuencia los Salmos predican a Cristo. Lo vimos más claramente en el Salmo 22, donde la cruz se describe mil años antes de que ocurriera, pero corre por todas partes: el Hombre bienaventurado del Salmo 1 se cumple en Jesús, el Rey de gloria del Salmo 24 entra como nuestro Redentor, y el Pastor del Salmo 23 da Su vida en Juan 10. El predicador que maneja un salmo con fidelidad, como Felipe con el etíope, comenzará desde el salmo y predicará a Jesús. Y porque los Salmos son tan honestos acerca de la emoción humana, dan al predicador permiso de abordar lo que la gente realmente siente el lunes por la mañana — temor, culpa, dolor, duda — y no solo lo que se supone que debe sentir.

blocks.en: 3. The Psalms in Pastoral Care
blocks.es_reference: 3. Los Salmos en el Cuidado Pastoral

blocks.en: If the Psalms are powerful in the pulpit, they are indispensable at the bedside. There is a reason a pastor reads Psalm 23 at gravesides "countless times over the years," as one of our lessons put it. In a moment when fresh words fail and well-meant explanations only irritate, the ancient cadences of "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me" reach a grieving heart in a way no original sermon can. The Psalms are tested words. They have comforted the dying for three thousand years, and they carry an authority and a familiarity that homemade comfort cannot match.
blocks.es_reference: Si los Salmos son poderosos en el púlpito, son indispensables junto al lecho. Hay una razón por la que un pastor lee el Salmo 23 junto a las tumbas "incontables veces a lo largo de los años," como lo expresó una de nuestras lecciones. En un momento en que las palabras nuevas fallan y las explicaciones bien intencionadas solo irritan, las antiguas cadencias de "Aunque ande en valle de sombra de muerte, no temeré mal alguno, porque tú estarás conmigo" alcanzan un corazón afligido de una manera que ningún sermón original puede. Los Salmos son palabras probadas. Han consolado a los moribundos por tres mil años, y llevan una autoridad y una familiaridad que el consuelo casero no puede igualar.

blocks.en: But using the Psalms in pastoral care is an art, not a formula. We learned from Joe Bayly's two visitors that the grieving usually need presence more than paragraphs; the Psalms are meant to be offered gently, in small doses, often simply read aloud and left to do their own work. Match the psalm to the wound. For the guilt-stricken, Psalm 51 and Psalm 103 speak of a God who forgives all our iniquities. For the frightened, Psalm 56 and Psalm 46 speak of a refuge. For the one crushed by loss, Psalm 55 invites the casting of the burden, and Psalm 42 gives honest words to a soul that thirsts and is downcast. Part of pastoral wisdom is knowing which psalm to open, and when simply to sit and let it be read.
blocks.es_reference: Pero usar los Salmos en el cuidado pastoral es un arte, no una fórmula. Aprendimos de los dos visitantes de Joe Bayly que el afligido suele necesitar presencia más que párrafos; los Salmos deben ofrecerse con suavidad, en pequeñas dosis, a menudo sencillamente leídos en voz alta y dejados a hacer su propia obra. Haga coincidir el salmo con la herida. Para el agobiado por la culpa, el Salmo 51 y el Salmo 103 hablan de un Dios que perdona todas nuestras iniquidades. Para el atemorizado, el Salmo 56 y el Salmo 46 hablan de un refugio. Para el aplastado por la pérdida, el Salmo 55 invita a echar la carga, y el Salmo 42 da palabras honestas a un alma que tiene sed y está abatida. Parte de la sabiduría pastoral es saber cuál salmo abrir, y cuándo simplemente sentarse y dejar que sea leído.

blocks.en: 4. The Psalms in Public Worship
blocks.es_reference: 4. Los Salmos en la Adoración Pública

blocks.en: The Psalms were Israel's songbook, and they remain a deep well for the worship of the church. They were written to be sung, and across the centuries the church has sung them, chanted them, paraphrased them into hymns, and prayed them responsively. To build worship around a psalm is to let Scripture itself set the agenda of praise — its words become our words, its God-centered honesty corrects our self-centered moods, and its sweep from lament to praise teaches a congregation the full range of the life of faith.
blocks.es_reference: Los Salmos fueron el cancionero de Israel, y siguen siendo un pozo profundo para la adoración de la iglesia. Fueron escritos para ser cantados, y a través de los siglos la iglesia los ha cantado, entonado, parafraseado en himnos, y orado de forma responsiva. Edificar la adoración en torno a un salmo es dejar que la Escritura misma fije la agenda de la alabanza — sus palabras se vuelven nuestras palabras, su honestidad centrada en Dios corrige nuestros estados de ánimo centrados en nosotros mismos, y su recorrido del lamento a la alabanza enseña a una congregación todo el rango de la vida de fe.

blocks.en: A psalm can shape an entire service: a call to worship drawn from its opening, a confession from its middle, an assurance from its turn toward hope, and a benediction from its close. The worship planner who learns to read a psalm this way will never run short of material, for the Psalter holds a song for every season of the soul — morning and evening, festival and funeral, triumph and tears.
blocks.es_reference: Un salmo puede dar forma a todo un culto: un llamado a la adoración tomado de su apertura, una confesión de su parte media, una seguridad de su giro hacia la esperanza, y una bendición de su cierre. El que planifica la adoración y aprende a leer un salmo así nunca se quedará sin material, pues el Salterio guarda un canto para cada estación del alma — mañana y tarde, fiesta y funeral, triunfo y lágrimas.

blocks.en: Application Exercise — Plan a Worship Experience: Take Psalm 19 and plan an innovative worship experience built around it. Include the music you would use, a brief discourse topic and outline, the Scripture you would read, and a complete, written-out invitation. The discourse need not be a traditional sermon. Then plan how that same psalm would shape worship in four very different settings: a campfire at a retreat; a Sunday morning service at First Baptist Church, Anywhere; a youth lock-in at midnight; and a Sunday-afternoon service in a prison. Notice how the unchanging psalm must be carried differently into each room — the same truth, freshly delivered to a different people.
blocks.es_reference: Ejercicio de Aplicación — Planifique una Experiencia de Adoración: Tome el Salmo 19 y planifique una experiencia de adoración innovadora construida en torno a él. Incluya la música que usaría, un breve tema y bosquejo de discurso, la Escritura que leería, y una invitación completa, escrita por entero. El discurso no tiene que ser un sermón tradicional. Luego planifique cómo ese mismo salmo daría forma a la adoración en cuatro escenarios muy distintos: una fogata en un retiro; un culto dominical en la Primera Iglesia Bautista de Cualquier Lugar; un encierro juvenil a medianoche; y un culto de domingo por la tarde en una prisión. Note cómo el salmo inmutable debe llevarse de manera distinta a cada sala — la misma verdad, entregada de nuevo a un pueblo diferente.

blocks.en: 5. The Psalms in Personal Devotion
blocks.es_reference: 5. Los Salmos en la Devoción Personal

blocks.en: Before the Psalms can be ministered to others, they must be lived by the minister. The danger of seminary study is that the Psalms become only texts to be analyzed, not prayers to be prayed. But these songs were given first for the closet, not the classroom.
blocks.es_reference: Antes de que los Salmos puedan ministrarse a otros, deben ser vividos por el ministro. El peligro del estudio del seminario es que los Salmos se vuelvan solo textos para analizar, no oraciones para orar. Pero estos cantos fueron dados primero para el aposento, no para el aula.

blocks.en: Psalm 1:2-3 (NKJV): "His delight is in the law of the LORD, and in His law he meditates day and night. He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water…"
blocks.es_reference: Salmo 1:2-3 (RVG): "En la ley de Jehová está su delicia, y en su ley medita de día y de noche. Será como árbol plantado junto a corrientes de aguas…"

blocks.en: Psalm 1 commends the man who meditates on God's law day and night, like a cow chewing the cud — turning the Word over and over until it nourishes the soul. Psalm 119, the longest chapter in the Bible, is one long love song to the Word hidden in the heart.
blocks.es_reference: El Salmo 1 elogia al hombre que medita en la ley de Dios día y noche, como una vaca que rumia — dando vueltas a la Palabra una y otra vez hasta que nutre el alma. El Salmo 119, el capítulo más largo de la Biblia, es una larga canción de amor a la Palabra guardada en el corazón.

blocks.en: The Psalms teach us that the heart of devotion is honesty before God. As one of our lessons put it, this book teaches us to be honest with God: if you are angry, say so; if you are afraid, bring it; if you are glad, express it. Every emotion a human being can feel is somewhere in the Psalms, brought openly into the presence of God. The minister who prays the Psalms daily will find his own heart kept tender, his fears stilled, his sins confessed, and his praise enlarged — and only out of that fullness can he truly feed others.
blocks.es_reference: Los Salmos nos enseñan que el corazón de la devoción es la honestidad delante de Dios. Como lo expresó una de nuestras lecciones, este libro nos enseña a ser honestos con Dios: si está enojado, dígalo; si tiene miedo, tráigalo; si está alegre, expréselo. Toda emoción que un ser humano pueda sentir está en algún lugar de los Salmos, traída abiertamente a la presencia de Dios. El ministro que ora los Salmos a diario hallará su propio corazón mantenido tierno, sus temores aquietados, sus pecados confesados, y su alabanza ampliada — y solo de esa plenitud puede alimentar verdaderamente a otros.

blocks.en: 6. Reading the Psalms Rightly
blocks.es_reference: 6. Leer los Salmos Correctamente

blocks.en: Because the Psalms are poetry, they must be read as poetry, and a few simple skills protect us from misusing them. First, watch for Hebrew parallelism — the way the second line of a verse echoes, intensifies, or contrasts the first. "The earth is the LORD's, and all its fullness" is answered by "the world and those who dwell therein"; the two lines say one thing twice for emphasis. Reading the lines together, rather than mining each for a separate point, keeps us close to the writer's meaning.
blocks.es_reference: Porque los Salmos son poesía, deben leerse como poesía, y unas pocas habilidades sencillas nos protegen de usarlos mal. Primero, observe el paralelismo hebreo — la manera en que la segunda línea de un versículo hace eco, intensifica o contrasta la primera. "De Jehová es la tierra y su plenitud" es respondido por "el mundo, y los que en él habitan"; las dos líneas dicen una cosa dos veces para énfasis. Leer las líneas juntas, en lugar de extraer de cada una un punto separado, nos mantiene cerca del significado del escritor.

blocks.en: Second, respect the kind of psalm before you. A lament like Psalm 22 or Psalm 42 moves through honest complaint toward renewed trust, and we must not rush it to the happy ending. A psalm of thanksgiving like Psalm 103 counts concrete benefits. A royal or messianic psalm like Psalm 24 points beyond its first occasion to Christ. Third, read every psalm in light of the whole of Scripture and ultimately in light of Jesus, in whom the deepest promises and the darkest cries alike find their answer. These are not academic niceties; they are the difference between feeding people the true sense of the text and feeding them our own invention.
blocks.es_reference: Segundo, respete la clase de salmo que tiene delante. Un lamento como el Salmo 22 o el Salmo 42 avanza por la queja honesta hacia la confianza renovada, y no debemos apresurarlo al final feliz. Un salmo de acción de gracias como el Salmo 103 cuenta beneficios concretos. Un salmo real o mesiánico como el Salmo 24 apunta más allá de su primera ocasión a Cristo. Tercero, lea cada salmo a la luz de toda la Escritura y, en última instancia, a la luz de Jesús, en quien tanto las promesas más profundas como los clamores más oscuros hallan su respuesta. Estas no son sutilezas académicas; son la diferencia entre alimentar a la gente con el verdadero sentido del texto y alimentarla con nuestra propia invención.

blocks.en: 7. A Word of Caution and Care
blocks.es_reference: 7. Una Palabra de Cautela y Cuidado

blocks.en: The very power of the Psalms calls for care in handling them. Their honesty can be misread: the angry and vengeful lines of some psalms are the raw prayers of sufferers handing their rage to God, not models for our own grudges, and they must be taught as such. Their comfort can be cheapened: to toss "all things work together for good" at a person in fresh grief, without presence and patience, can wound rather than heal. And their promises must be read truly — Psalm 23 does not promise a life without valleys, only a Shepherd within them; Psalm 103 does not promise that every disease is healed in this life, for some of God's choicest servants, like Paul, were left with their thorn.
blocks.es_reference: El poder mismo de los Salmos exige cuidado en su manejo. Su honestidad puede malinterpretarse: las líneas airadas y vengativas de algunos salmos son las oraciones crudas de los que sufren entregando su ira a Dios, no modelos para nuestros propios rencores, y deben enseñarse como tales. Su consuelo puede abaratarse: arrojar "todas las cosas ayudan a bien" a una persona en duelo reciente, sin presencia ni paciencia, puede herir en lugar de sanar. Y sus promesas deben leerse con verdad — el Salmo 23 no promete una vida sin valles, solo un Pastor dentro de ellos; el Salmo 103 no promete que toda enfermedad sea sanada en esta vida, pues algunos de los siervos más escogidos de Dios, como Pablo, quedaron con su aguijón.

blocks.en: The minister of the Psalms, then, must be both bold and humble: bold to bring these tested words into every situation, and humble enough to let them say what they actually say. Handled rightly, the Psalms will never run dry. They will preach, comfort, lead worship, and feed the soul long after our own clever words are forgotten.
blocks.es_reference: El ministro de los Salmos, entonces, debe ser a la vez audaz y humilde: audaz para traer estas palabras probadas a cada situación, y bastante humilde para dejar que digan lo que en realidad dicen. Manejados correctamente, los Salmos nunca se secarán. Predicarán, consolarán, guiarán la adoración, y alimentarán el alma mucho después de que nuestras propias palabras ingeniosas sean olvidadas.

blocks.en: 8. Carrying the Songs Forward
blocks.es_reference: 8. Llevar los Cantos Adelante

blocks.en: We began this course by calling the Psalms the folk songs of the Bible — the people's songs, sung in every key of human experience and always in the presence of God. The aim of all our study has been not merely to understand these songs but to be able to sing them with others and for others: to put their words in the mouths of the grieving, to lift them over a congregation, to whisper them at a deathbed, and to pray them in the secret place. That is the Psalms in ministry.
blocks.es_reference: Comenzamos este curso llamando a los Salmos las canciones del pueblo de la Biblia — los cantos del pueblo, cantados en cada tono de la experiencia humana y siempre en la presencia de Dios. El propósito de todo nuestro estudio no ha sido meramente entender estos cantos, sino poder cantarlos con otros y para otros: poner sus palabras en la boca del afligido, elevarlos sobre una congregación, susurrarlos junto a un lecho de muerte, y orarlos en el lugar secreto. Eso es los Salmos en el ministerio.

blocks.en: In our final unit we will draw the whole course together and consider what it means to carry these songs through a lifetime of service — how the Psalms accompany the believer from the morning of faith to its evening, and how the minister who has lived in them becomes, like the tree of Psalm 1, planted by the rivers of water, bringing forth fruit in season for the good of God's people. For now, take up the Psalms not only as a book you have studied, but as a ministry you have been given.
blocks.es_reference: En nuestra unidad final reuniremos todo el curso y consideraremos qué significa llevar estos cantos a través de toda una vida de servicio — cómo los Salmos acompañan al creyente desde la mañana de la fe hasta su atardecer, y cómo el ministro que ha vivido en ellos llega a ser, como el árbol del Salmo 1, plantado junto a corrientes de aguas, dando fruto en su tiempo para el bien del pueblo de Dios. Por ahora, tome los Salmos no solo como un libro que ha estudiado, sino como un ministerio que se le ha dado.

sa.prompt: Explain the shift these capstone units make, and why the lesson says the Psalms uniquely speak FOR us.
sa.model: These final two capstone units make a shift from asking what a psalm means to asking how to carry the Psalms into ministry and life. The earlier units interpreted; these units put the Psalms to work. The lesson says the Psalms uniquely speak FOR us: while most of Scripture is God speaking to us, the Psalms are largely words addressed to God, and so they put language in our mouths when we have none of our own. They give the grieving words for grief, the thankful words for praise, and the frightened words for trust. That is why they are such a gift for ministry, for they voice the cry of the human heart before God.

sa.prompt: Explain how a psalm should be preached, including finding its dominant emotion and preaching Christ.
sa.model: A psalm should be preached differently from a logical letter of Paul. Rather than tracing a tight argument, the preacher finds the psalm's single dominant emotion or claim and makes that the center, letting the message carry the same feeling the psalm carries. Psalm 23 is not six unrelated points about sheep but one great assurance: the LORD is my shepherd, therefore I shall not want. And like Philip beginning at Isaiah and preaching Jesus to the Ethiopian, the faithful preacher begins at the psalm's text and preaches Christ from it, showing how the psalm finally points to Him. Preach the psalm's heart, and preach it toward Jesus.

sa.prompt: Explain why the Psalms are indispensable in pastoral care and how Psalm 23 functions at gravesides.
sa.model: The Psalms are indispensable in pastoral care because they are tested words, having comforted the dying and the grieving for three thousand years. They carry an authority and a depth that our own improvised comfort lacks. Psalm 23 in particular functions at gravesides as almost no other words can: its ancient cadences reach the dying and the bereaved when fresh words fail, speaking peace into the very valley of the shadow of death. When a minister has nothing adequate of his own to say, he can open the Psalms and let words proven over millennia do what his own cannot, carrying God's comfort into the hardest moments of life.

sa.prompt: Explain what it means to 'match the psalm to the wound,' giving examples from the lesson.
sa.model: To "match the psalm to the wound" is to choose the psalm whose theme fits the particular need of the person before us, rather than offering the same words for every situation. The lesson gives examples: for the fearful, a psalm of refuge like Psalm 56; for the crushed and overwhelmed, Psalm 55 with its call to cast the burden; for the guilt-stricken, Psalm 51 and Psalm 103 on the God who forgives all our iniquities. Just as a physician matches the remedy to the ailment, the wise minister knows the Psalms well enough to bring the right one to the right wound, so that Scripture speaks directly to the person's real need.

sa.prompt: Explain how the Psalms serve public worship and how a single psalm can shape a whole service.
sa.model: The Psalms serve public worship by giving the congregation God-given words of praise, confession, and trust, and by letting Scripture itself set the agenda of worship rather than our shifting moods. A single psalm can shape an entire service: the lesson shows how its parts can supply a call to worship, a confession of sin, an assurance of pardon, and a benediction, all drawn from the one psalm. Built this way, worship is corrected and deepened, because the psalm leads the people to praise God for who He truly is rather than merely expressing how they happen to feel that day.

sa.prompt: Describe the Psalm 19 worship-planning exercise, including the four settings students must plan for.
sa.model: The Psalm 19 worship-planning exercise asks the student to take that one psalm and design a worship experience around it, then plan how it would work in four very different settings: a retreat campfire, a Sunday morning service, a midnight youth lock-in, and a prison service. The point is to learn that the same psalm can be brought faithfully to vastly different people and places, with the form adjusted while the truth stays the same. It trains the minister to think practically about leading worship from the Psalms, shaping the setting, tone, and presentation to the congregation while letting the psalm itself carry the message.

sa.prompt: Explain the danger and the goal of the Psalms in the minister's personal devotion.
sa.model: The danger in a minister's personal devotion is that seminary study can turn the Psalms into mere texts to analyze rather than prayers to pray; the very training that equips him can quietly starve his own soul if the Psalms become only professional material. The goal is the opposite: that the Psalms remain his own prayers, the language of his personal walk with God. He must keep praying them, not only studying them, bringing his own heart honestly before God in their words. The lesson warns that handling holy things for others is no substitute for being fed by them oneself; the Psalms must stay devotional, not just academic.

sa.prompt: Explain the reading skills the lesson gives: parallelism, respecting the psalm type, and reading via Christ.
sa.model: The lesson gives several reading skills. First, watch for Hebrew parallelism, the way a psalm's second line echoes, intensifies, or contrasts the first, which is the basic music of Hebrew poetry and often carries the meaning. Second, respect the psalm's type: a lament moves differently from a hymn of praise, and we must read each according to its kind. Third, read every psalm finally through Christ, since the Psalms point to Him and find their fullest meaning in Him. Together these skills keep us from misreading the Psalms and help us hear what each one is actually saying and where it ultimately leads.

sa.prompt: Explain the cautions the lesson gives: misreading honesty, cheapening comfort, and reading promises truly.
sa.model: The lesson gives three cautions. First, do not misread the Psalms' honesty: their raw, even angry words are the prayers of sufferers handing their rage to God, not models licensing our own grudges. Second, do not cheapen their comfort: we must not rush a lament like Psalm 22 or 42 to its happy ending, but respect the honest movement through complaint toward renewed trust. Third, read the promises truly: Psalm 23 promises not a life without valleys but a Shepherd within them. Each caution guards against twisting the Psalms into something easier or more comfortable than what they actually say, so we handle them with integrity.

sa.prompt: According to the close, what has been the aim of the whole course, and what does it mean to carry the songs forward?
sa.model: According to the close, the aim of the whole course has been not merely to study the Psalms but to learn to carry them into a life of ministry and faith. To carry the songs forward means to take these psalms we have studied and use them: to preach them, to bring them to the bedside and the graveside, to build worship around them, and to pray them as our own. They are not a subject we finish and set aside but a lifelong companion and tool for serving others and walking with God. The course ends by sending the student out to keep these songs alive in real ministry.
